question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}120 & ≡13\cdot 9+3\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡13\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ 140 & ≡15\cdot 9+5\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡15\cdot 0+5\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}120\cdot 140 & ≡3\cdot 5\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡15\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡9+6\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡0+6\, & (\text{mod}\,9) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
120\cdot 140\text{ mod }9=6.
$$
